items: Covers Section 5: Direction Sense spatial reasoning concepts.
Includes a dedicated Answer Key section for self-assessment and verification.

Concept:

Coding–Decoding questions test the ability to understand a fixed pattern or logic used to convert a word or number into another form. In SSC, coding questions are generally simple and based on letter positions or alphabet shifting.

Common Types in SSC:

1. Letter Position Coding (A = 1, B = 2 … Z = 26)

2. Alphabet Shifting (forward or backward)

3. Word Coding (same pattern applied to all words)

Method to Solve:

1. Observe the pattern in the given coded pair.

2. Identify the position change or shift.

3. Apply the same logic to the new word.

blocks.content:
Solved Examples:

Example 1:

If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded?

Logic: C→D, A→B, T→U (each letter shifted by +1)

Answer: EPH

Example 2:

If PEN is written as 16–5–14, how is INK written?

Logic: Alphabet positions

I = 9, N = 14, K = 11

Answer: 9–14–11

Practice Questions (Coding–Decoding):



Q1. If BOOK is coded as CPPL, how is PEN coded?

A. QFO B. QFM C. OFM D. PFN



Q2. If A = 1, B = 2 … Z = 26, what is the code for BAD?

A. 2–1–4 B. 1–2–4 C. 2–4–1 D. 4–2–1



Q3. If LION is written as KHMN, how is BEAR written?

A. ADZQ B. ADAQ C. ADZP D. ZCZQ

Spatial orientation, cardinal points, and distance evaluation

items:
Concept:

Direction sense questions test the ability to track movement and direction from a starting point. SBIquestions are usually GUIDE, direct and involve one or two turns.

Key Rules:

• Always fix North before solving

• Right turn = clockwise

• Left turn = anti-clockwise

blocks.content:
Solved Examples:

Example 1:

A person walks 10 m north, then turns right and walks 5 m.

Direction faced now: East

Example 2:

A man walks 5 m east, then 5 m south, then 5 m west.

Distance from starting point: 5 m

items: Coding–Decoding questions frequently feature letter-shifting, direct coding, and symbol substitution patterns.
Direction Sense problems routinely test cardinal directions and shortest distance calculations using the Pythagoras theorem.

blocks.content:
Practice Questions (Direction Sense):



Q4. A person walks 10 m south, then turns left and walks 5 m. Which direction is he facing now?

A. North B. South C. East D. West



Q5. A man walks 5 m north, then 5 m east, then 5 m south. How far is he from the starting point?

A. 0 m B. 5 m C. 10 m D. 15 m



Q6. A woman walks 10 m east, turns right, walks 10 m, turns right again and walks 10 m. Which direction is she facing now?

A. East B. West C. North D. South
Q1. B   Q2. A   Q3. B   Q4. D   Q5. B   Q6. B
